title: Fibre-product compatible tuples form a module sheaf on an algebraic-space etale site
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $(q_i:V_i\to F)_{i\in I}$ a set-indexed family of etale maps from schemes, not necessarily jointly surjective. Work in a universe containing $I$, all section sets and the products below, and a small skeleton of $F_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $R_{ij}=V_i\times_F V_j$, with projections $p_i,p_j$; all displayed fibre products are schemes by the representable diagonal. Let $L_i$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_{(V_i)_{\mathrm{et}}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Restrictions to overlaps are restrictions on localized etale sites. For every pair let $a_{ij}:L_j|_{(R_{ij})_{\mathrm{et}}}\to L_i|_{(R_{ij})_{\mathrm{et}}}$ be a module-sheaf morphism. No invertibility, diagonal identity or cocycle is assumed. For $W\to F$ in $F_{\mathrm{et}}$, put $W_i=W\times_FV_i$ and $W_{ij}=W\times_FV_i\times_FV_j$, with the indicated maps to $V_i$ and $R_{ij}$. Then $H_i(W)=L_i(W_i)$ and $K_{ij}(W)=L_i(W_{ij})$, with restrictions induced by fibre products, are sheaves of sets on $F_{\mathrm{et}}$. The two maps $\prod_iH_i\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}K_{ij}$ with coordinates $s_i|_{W_{ij}}$ and $a_{ij}(s_j|_{W_{ij}})$ are morphisms of sheaves. Their equalizer is the sheaf with exact section formula
$$M(W)=\{(s_i)\in\prod_i L_i(W_i):s_i|_{W_{ij}}=a_{ij}(s_j|_{W_{ij}})\text{ for all }i,j\}.$$
It is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_F$-modules with zero, addition and additive inverses coordinatewise and scalar action $(b(s_i))_i=((b|_{W_i})s_i)_i$ for $b\in\mathcal O_F(W)$. Restriction along $W'\to W$ is coordinatewise section restriction and is semilinear over $\mathcal O_F(W)\to\mathcal O_F(W')$. These formulas define the object and its module structure, without assuming $F$ is a scheme or an object of its own small etale site.

proof.text: For two etale scheme objects U and V, apply the scheme-test representability in IsEtale(U → F) to V → F. It supplies a scheme P, an etale projection p : P → V, and a Yoneda pullback square. The scheme-morphism test makes yoneda.map p etale, and composition with V → F makes P an object of the etale site. Lift the other projection through the fully faithful Yoneda functor. The pullback universal property, transported by Yoneda, gives the binary-product cone in the full subcategory of etale objects. This is the Lean proof of etaleSite_hasBinaryProducts.

Use the explicitly defined tupleChartSheaf and tupleOverlapSheaf: they are Mathlib pushforwards of module sheaves along Over.star and Over.map, with scalar restriction along the projection to W. Their sheaf condition and localization continuity are already supplied by the existing general-site module-sheaf infrastructure; no separate algebraic-space covering lemma is needed.

Evaluation of module sheaves followed by forgetting to sets preserves the two products. Compare the evaluated limiting fan with the literal type-theoretic dependent product fan. Its unique comparison isomorphism has exactly the canonical projections as coordinates, proving the two coordinate maps bijective.

For p : U → T, the adjunction Over.forget T ⊣ Over.star T constructs tupleRestriction. Its composite with the projection to W is prod.snd, by the inverse law of the adjunction hom equivalence. This equation and the over-category commuting triangle prove naturality. Apply the local module restriction to this natural family of arrows; semilinearity and the projection equation prove linearity over O(W). The resulting tupleChartRestriction is a module-sheaf morphism. Take its composites with chart-product projections and, on the right, the pushforward of a_ij. The product universal property supplies f and g, whose coordinate formulas follow from Pi.lift_π. No identity or cocycle is used.

Evaluation and forgetting preserve the equalizer, so comparison with the subtype equalizer in Type identifies its section set with {s : P(W) | f(s) = g(s)}. The injective overlap coordinates identify this equality with all the specified compatibility equations. Restrict the bijective chart coordinate map to these equivalent predicates and compose the two equivalences. Its underlying tuple is definitionally the chart coordinates of the equalizer inclusion. The underlying-set functor also preserves this equalizer as a cone of sheaves.

The pinned equivalence reduces zero, addition, negation and scalar formulas to linearity of the equalizer inclusion and chart-product projections; the scalar structure of each pushforward is restriction along prod.snd. Naturality of the same inclusion and projections gives the coordinate restriction formula. Semilinearity of the equalizer module presheaf gives the last formula. The proof works for an empty family as well.

lean.note: Uses the recorded algebraic-space small etale site and localized module categories. The chart and overlap sheaves, canonical restriction arrows, products, and literal compatible-tuple section subtype are explicit constructions. The main theorem gives the two maps by their exact coordinates, their underlying-set equalizer, its canonical section bijections, and all operation/restriction formulas. The auxiliary binary-product existence theorem states the representability clause of this node; its universal property determines the products up to unique isomorphism. No covering or cocycle assumption, no evaluation at F, and no statement correction.

Hypotheses: arbitrary family V : I → F.EtaleSite, localized module sheaves L, arbitrary a_ij : L_j|R → L_i|R in the right direction, diagonal pairs included, no cover/cocycle/invertibility/Nonempty/Fintype assumption. H_i and K_ij are pushforwards along Over.star; the restriction arrow comes from the fibre-product universal property, not a choice. Bijective product coordinates determine f and g. Equalizer has a limit statement in sheaves of sets and a uniquely pinned bijection with the literal compatible-tuple set; zero/add/neg/scalar/restriction/semilinearity are coordinatewise. The sorry theorem that the étale site has binary products is the node's own fibre-product claim; it is true and no competing instance exists. Edge cases: empty index set gives 0; non-covering families allowed; a=0 or id on one chart gives 0 or L; F never evaluated. Module universe max(u+1) v is the containing universe the node stipulates (it includes the site skeleton).
